brief.summary: A course messaging tool for a university's undergraduate data visualization class, where students and teaching staff discuss figure drafts in threads tied to specific assignments and revisions.
brief.user: Tomás Herrera, a second-year PhD student in information science working as one of three teaching assistants for COGS 127 'Visualizing Data' (164 enrolled students). He is fluent in visualization theory and grades about 55 students.
brief.moment: It is Thursday evening and Assignment 4 ('Redesign a misleading public figure'), is due Monday at 11:59 pm. Since this morning 23 messages have come in from his section. Some are quick questions ('can we use a log scale?'), others are students who attached a revised draft and want to know whether they addressed last week's feedback. He is working through the unanswered ones: replying in each thread, referencing the student's earlier revision, pointing to a common problem he is seeing (truncated y-axes), and deciding which questions are general enough to answer once for all 164 students instead of one by one. One student, Aisha Bello, has asked twice since Tuesday and is still waiting.

I need the front end for Critique Commons. A course messaging tool for a university's undergraduate data visualization class, where students and teaching staff discuss figure drafts in threads tied to specific assignments and revisions.

Who's using it: Tomás Herrera, a second-year PhD student in information science working as one of three teaching assistants for COGS 127 'Visualizing Data' (164 enrolled students). He is fluent in visualization theory and grades about 55 students.

Some are quick questions ('can we use a log scale?'), others are students who attached a revised draft and want to know whether they addressed last week's feedback. One student, Aisha Bello, has asked twice since Tuesday and is still waiting.

What's in the system at this point: Section B roster: 54 students. 23 unread or unanswered messages, oldest from Tuesday 2:14 pm. Each thread is tied to an assignment (A1–A4) and contains the student's draft image uploads by revision (e.g. 'A4 draft v2, uploaded Wed 9:41 pm, 1.2 MB PNG'), prior TA comments, and the rubric criteria in question (encoding choice, axis integrity, labeling, color accessibility). 4 course-wide announcements already posted by Professor Lindqvist. Office hours: Fri 1–3 pm. A saved reply 'Truncated axis explainer' has been used 9 times this term. Average TA response time this week: 14 hours.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
